column3: [warm, motherly, smiling] Good news, everyone! Rations are being handed out right now. Come along, and don't forget your card.
[firm, composed, still kind] A little inspection, nothing to worry about. Stand still, papers out, and it'll be over before you know it.
[firm, composed, still kind] Bedtime, everyone. Curfew starts now: home you go, and stay there till morning.
[stern, cold, slowly] The city is in lockdown. Stay inside. I am not asking.
[stern, cold, slowly] Civil Protection is visiting one of our blocks. Cooperate, and everyone sleeps soundly tonight.
[warm, motherly, smiling] A supply convoy is coming through! Step aside and let it pass, there's a love.
[warm, motherly, smiling] That's all done. Thank you, everyone. Back to your day.
[warm, motherly, smiling] In just a couple of minutes, rations! Start making your way over, dears.
[firm, composed, still kind] Curfew in two minutes. Finish up and head home, please.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Everything is calm again. Well done, all of you.
[firm, composed, still kind] Things are a little tense. Papers ready, heads down, and we'll get through it.
[stern, cold, slowly] We are on red. Go home. Whatever happens out there now, you were warned.

[furious, barely controlled, clipped] Citizens. The city has been overrun by its own ingratitude. Go indoors and stay there. Anyone in the open will be fired upon from the Nexus. This is not a request.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Good morning, everyone! Rise and shine: a brand new day for the city.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Halfway through the day. Keep it up, I'm proud of you.
[warm, motherly, smiling] The day's nearly done. Finish up, and think about heading home.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Goodnight, everyone. Sleep well, and dream of the city.
[firm, composed, still kind] Something has got out of the infestation. Keep away from it and let the crews do their work.
[firm, composed, still kind] A little power cut, nothing more. The crews are on it, so stay calm.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Lights back on! Thank you for your patience.
[stern, cold, slowly] Overwatch is dealing with some trouble. Stay well away from it.
[stern, cold, slowly] Overwatch is cleaning up a troubled corner of the city. Let them work.
[stern, cold, slowly] A response team is on its way. Please don't get in their way.
[furious, barely controlled, clipped] Some people have run from where they belong. If you see them, tell a unit. Now.
[stern, cold, slowly] Overwatch soldiers are arriving. Make way for them.
[stern, cold, slowly] We're checking one of our housing blocks. Stay in your room and it'll be quick.
[firm, composed, still kind] Some troublemakers are spreading out. Don't go near them, and don't listen to them.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Welcome to the city, all you new faces! Civil Intake is just this way.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Hello, and welcome to the city! You're going to love it here.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Remember, a good citizen is a happy citizen. And I do so want you all to be happy.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Morning, everyone! Shoes on: time for our little jog.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Into the yard, everyone, for our morning exercises. Stretch!
[warm, motherly, smiling] Parade time! Chins up, shoulders back, and let's show the city who we are.
[furious, barely controlled, clipped] So you have come for me. Come, then. You will not reach me.
[stern, cold, slowly] It is over. The city is mine again, and I will remember every one of you.
[furious, barely controlled, clipped] They have silenced the Nexus. It changes nothing.
[warm, motherly, smiling] My dear citizens, I am going to speak to you all in a few minutes. Come and gather in front of the stand. I would so hate to miss anyone.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Citizens. Thank you for coming to hear me. Let us talk about the days behind us.
[firm, composed, still kind] Blood has been spilled in our streets. Every life lost to violence is stolen from all of us. Violence solves nothing. It only invites more.
[firm, composed, still kind] Civil Protection has been busy. No one taken to the cells was taken at random. They chose disorder, and disorder has a price.
[warm, motherly, smiling] To those of you who came forward and told us what you saw: thank you. You know who you are, and so do I. Your loyalty will not be forgotten.

[stern, cold, slowly] Some of you were hurt for helping the city, beaten in the dark by cowards who call themselves liberators. Look at what they do to their own neighbours, and ask who your friends really are.
[stern, cold, slowly] Citizens have been taken, dragged off by the so-called Resistance and questioned like animals. That is the freedom they offer you: a cage, and a chair.
[stern, cold, slowly] Some who were held have run from where they belong. They will be found. And whoever hides them will stand beside them when they are.
[firm, composed, still kind] Someone has been defacing the city's notices. A poster costs the Union very little. Replacing it will cost you your rations.
[firm, composed, still kind] There has been stealing, from the city and from each other. A thief steals from everyone standing in this square.
[firm, composed, still kind] Voices have been raised at the officers who keep you safe. I understand frustration. I will not tolerate it in the street.
[stern, cold, slowly] Machines have been broken and the city's work undone. Sabotage hurts no one but you. It is your water, your light, your bread.
[firm, composed, still kind] Some of you have seen our officers act firmly. Firmness is a kindness, in the end. It ends trouble before trouble ends you.
[warm, motherly, smiling] I hear some of you have found comfort in a bottle. I do not blame you. But a clear head is a loyal head.
[warm, motherly, smiling] And I have seen good things too: neighbours sharing their bread, calming each other's nerves. That is the city I am proud of.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Some of you have lost hope. Do not. Hope is not something you are given. It is something you choose, every morning.
[stern, cold, slowly] There are those among you who whisper of freedom and mean only chaos. Every one of them you shelter is a debt your whole block will pay.
[warm, motherly, smiling] I know the rations have been thin. I feel every empty bowl as if it were my own. Work your shifts, keep your quotas, and the trains will come.
[firm, composed, still kind] Let me be clear, so no one can say they were not told. The rules of this city are not suggestions, and my authority is not in question.
[warm, motherly, smiling] I see tired faces, and I understand. But the lights are on, the streets are swept, and not one of you is alone.
[warm, motherly, smiling] These have been quiet days, days of order and honest work. The Union sees it. I see it.
[warm, motherly, smiling] I can see fear in your faces. You have nothing to fear from me. Only from those who would set you against me.
[firm, composed, still kind] There is a restlessness in this city. I feel it. Restlessness can be turned into work, or into ruin. Choose work.
[warm, motherly, smiling] You look well: rested, fed and calm. Good. Keep it so.
[warm, motherly, smiling] Now go back to your work, and remember: this city is only as strong as each one of you. Glory to the Union.

[low, urgent] Listen.
[tired, flat] Look.
[tired, flat] Look.
[pleading, quietly] Please.
[pleading, quietly] Please.
[whispers, tense] Keep your voice down.
[whispers, tense] Keep your voice down.

[thinking it over] Well...

[sharp, low] You.

[cold, flat] What do you want?

[wary, guarded] Do I know you?

[tired, dry] Hey. Still here, huh? [exhales] Me too.

[nervous, too polite] No trouble here, officer.

[flat, tired] I should get going.

[hesitant] Maybe. I'd have to think about it.

[plain, tired] Yeah. All right.

[warm, a small smile] For you? Of course.

[tired, dismissive] You're asking the wrong person.

[hushed, uneasy] I can't talk about that. You know why.

[guarded, flat] I wouldn't know anything about that.

[frightened, quick] I don't know, and I don't want to know.

[low, careful] I've heard things. [pause] Everyone has.

[quiet, grim] Honestly? [sighs] It's as bad as it looks.

[tight, barely holding it in] I've had about all I can take.

[worn, matter of fact] Getting by. That's all I can do.

[quiet, hopeful] It can't last forever. Nothing ever does.

[weak, hollow] I haven't had a real meal in days.

[soft, grateful] It's good to just talk to someone.
[hollow, defeated] What's the point? [pause] Really, what is the point?
[hollow, defeated] What's the point? [pause] Really, what is the point?
[frightened, hushed] I'm scared. Aren't you?
[frightened, hushed] I'm scared. Aren't you?
[exhausted] I'm tired. [sighs] Just so tired.
[exhausted] I'm tired. [sighs] Just so tired.
[dry, low] You're not wrong.
[dry, low] You're not wrong.
[even, firm] Well, I don't see it that way.
[even, firm] Well, I don't see it that way.
[stung, stiff] Hey. There's no need for that.
[stung, stiff] Hey. There's no need for that.
[short laugh] Ha. [warm, surprised] That's the first laugh I've had all week.
[short laugh] Ha. [warm, surprised] That's the first laugh I've had all week.
[nervous, backing down] I'm sorry. I didn't mean anything by it.
[nervous, backing down] I'm sorry. I didn't mean anything by it.

[sincere, quietly] Thank you. I won't forget it.

[moved, voice catching] You didn't have to do that. Thank you.

[frightened, hands up] I don't want any trouble.

[whispers] Careful. The walls have ears.

[low, warning] Stay away from the units today. They're in a mood.

[earnest, a little rehearsed] The Administrator knows best. Everyone knows that!

[alarmed, hushed] You shouldn't say things like that. Someone will hear.

[tired, kindly] Keep your head down and do what they say. That's how you make it.

[under their breath] Not with them standing right there.

[afraid, firm] I've got people to think about. Leave me out of it.

[quiet, a hint of a smile] Whoever they are, good luck to them.

[uneasy, low] There's gonna be trouble tonight. I can feel it.

[desperate, quietly] I need help. I've got nobody else to ask.

[loud, accusing, pointing] That one! That one talks to Civil Protection!

[panicked, loud] That's a lie! I never told them anything!

[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] Step aside. Or end it ... yourself. Choose.
[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] Time is a luxury you no longer have, Administrator.
[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] Choose. Or I will ... choose for you.
[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] A wise choice, Administrator.
[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] ... As you wish.
[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] Your citizens sleep poorly. They wake ... prepared.
[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] Even the lights are leaving you.
[slow, breathy, unsettling calm, odd pauses and emphasis] It ends where it began, Administrator. In your office.
[slow, breathy, patient, faintly amused] I will ask ... once more.
[slow, soft, mock regret] She was given a choice. [pause] She chose ... poorly.
[slow, pleased, breathy] Then it is ... decided.
[slow, courteous, cold] Congratulations ... Administrator. We will be ... watching.
[barely a whisper, amused] Not yet.
[slow, breathy, approving] A wise ... investment.
[very slow, soft, dreamlike] Rise ... and listen.
[slow, fading] Remember this ... when you wake.
[slow, dry, faintly disappointed] How ... disappointing. Another time, then.
[slow, satisfied, breathy] The city ... thanks you. In its way.
[slow, businesslike] Time, I think ... to resume.
[slow, cold, quiet] My employers ... are not patient.
